messages:
jordan: Quick check — opened a tiny TF change moving KMS access from inline key policy to aws_kms_grant for the IRSA role. Staging started failing to decrypt mounted secrets after deploy. Anyone seen a propagation hole when switching to grants?

anika: @jordan can you paste the TF snippet and the pod error? usually either grant principal mismatch or timing.

jordan: error in sidecar logs: \"AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource\". TF: ```resource \"aws_kms_grant\" \"irsa_decrypt\" {\n  name            = \"irsa-decrypt-${var.env}\"\n  key_id          = aws_kms_key.secrets.id\n  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.irsa_role.arn\n  operations      = [\"Decrypt\"]\n}\n```

kyle: hmm we usually use the role ARN for grantee_principal and that works. Did you switch the key policy to remove the role allow? grants are additive but if you removed a statement that allowed the role and rely only on the grant, note grants are ephemeral and tied to the principal's AWS account/principal id.

jordan: I did remove an old policy entry that explicitly allowed the role. Thought the grant would be enough.

sam: Grants are fine but IRSA uses AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity -> sessions. KMS checks the session principal (role session, not assumed-by). Typically grants target the role principal ARN; however there are corner cases with external IDs/session names. Also cross-account keys need principal as AWS principal, not an STS session.

anika: Also a gotcha: if the role was just created by TF in the same apply, the grant might be created before the role ARN fully propagates in the KMS service and the grant call ends up referencing a principal that KMS doesn't yet recognize. Ordering can bite.

jordan: right — I did a single apply. Is best practice here to split into two applies or to use a depends_on?

kyle: depends_on can help if TF resource order supports it, but aws_kms_grant is an API call that will still fail if the role isn't fully usable. I usually do: 1) apply role + policy, 2) run a follow-up apply for grants. Alternatively, create aws_iam_role first and then run a null_resource local-exec that waits and then creates grant via aws cli.

jordan: if we do follow-up apply, what's the smallest check to confirm grant is active? is there a way to validate via AWS CLI?

sam: yes — run `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-id>` and grep for the granteePrincipal. Also try `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://test.ct` as the role (assume role) to verify. For quick test: `aws sts assume-role --role-arn <role-arn> --role-session-name test-decrypt` then export temporary creds and run `aws kms decrypt ...`

anika: another quick workaround: keep the key policy statement allowing the role ARN in place (least risky) and add the grant later for better auditability. That way pods don't break during TF rollouts.

jordan: good plan. One more weirdness — staging pods show the role ARN in logs but decrypt still fails immediately after apply. Could this be a cache on the KMS side?

kyle: there can be short eventual consistency. If you create the grant immediately after role creation, KMS might return success but still reject the first decrypt attempts until internal replication finishes. Adding a short retry/backoff in the secret fetcher sidecar (5-10s x 6) helped us before.

infra-bot: deploy 2101eb3 completed for service/secret-agent on staging at 2026-03-17T09:12:02Z — pods restarted.

jordan: thanks everyone. Action items: (1) revert removal of policy statement for role on the key (temporary), (2) split TF change into role+policy apply then grant apply, (3) add retry backoff to secret-agent sidecar, (4) add a CI smoke: `sts assume-role` + `kms decrypt` using test ciphertext. I'll open a PR for the CI test and a follow-up apply run.

anika: ping me on the PR, I can help with the CI script.

kyle: FYI if you want a short lived script that waits for grant to show up: ```for i in {1..20}; do aws kms list-grants --key-id $KID | grep $ROLE && break || sleep 3; done```

jordan: added TODOs to the branch. will do the staged apply tonight. thanks :thumbsup:
